Q: Tahnk you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, but you can reference the claim.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in League City, Texas, turning left at an intersection with a green light, or at least I thought it was green.
Q: What direction were you traveling before the turn?
A: I was heading north on the main road and wanted to get into the parking lot on the left side.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you started your turn?
A: I saw headlights coming toward me, but they seemed far enough away. I didn't think it was a problem.
Q: How fast were you going when you began the turn?
A: Not fast, maybe walking speed through the intersection. I was careful about it.
Q: What happened next?
A: The other car came through the intersection faster than I expected and hit the front passenger side of my car.
Q: Did the airbags deploy, or did you hit anything else?
A: The airbags didn't go off, but the impact threw me against the seatbelt and the steering wheel.
Q: Did you seek medical attention afterward?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same evening. They said I had a back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a
referral for physical therapy.
Q: Are you still experiencing pain or limtied movement?
A: Yes, my lower back is stiff, especially in the morning, and bending over is uncomfortable. I've been going to
therapy twice a week.
Q: Has anyone else been in the vehicle with you?
A: No, I was alone in the car.
Q: Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I believe I had the right of way on the turn, and I want my injuries taken seriously.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>
